text:
Marisol: quick q — we're staging a model-variant rollout next week. plan is staged fanout by tier (free/paid/enterprise/partner). worried about a fallback storm in smaller regions where the new variant OOMs or runs out of capacity. any ideas?

Davin: can we make fallback scoped per-tier so enterprise fallbacks don't spill into free pool? last time spill caused throttles.

Priya: Router today has only global fallback buckets. Per-tier scoping exists in the control plane rollout spec but router ignores it at decision time.

Alex: core debate: do we make fallback decisions at router (fast, local) or ask control-plane for policy (accurate, has quotas but adds RTT)?

Davin: For soft rollouts we need latency-sensitive decision path. Router should use a compact policy blob that includes per-tier fallback targets and max-fallback-rate. control plane publishes that via config push.

Priya: +1. Also add per-region caps: a tier might be 5% globally but 0% in APAC if no capacity.

Marisol: example policy sketch:

```
rollout:
  variant: v2
  percent_by_tier:
    enterprise: 20
    paid: 5
    free: 1
  fallback_policy:
    scope: per-tier
    per_tier_targets:
      enterprise: v1
      paid: v1
      free: v1
    max_fallback_rate: 0.1
    region_overrides:
      apac:
        paid: 0
```

Davin: router can enforce max_fallback_rate and track a rolling counter per (tier,region,variant). that prevents cascade.

ops-bot: ALERT metric fallback_count increased by 3.2x in eu-west-2 for paid tier at 14:12 UTC

Alex: can we rely on router counters for alerting? we need them exported as telemetry with labels: tier,region,from_variant,to_variant,fallback_reason

Priya: agree — add metric name `redwood.router.fallbacks_total` with labels {tier,region,from,to,reason}. we should expose rate and percent_of_requests.

Marisol: also need dashboard panels: per-tier rollout coverage, fallback-rate heatmap, cost delta when fallback occurs (because v1 cheaper than v2), and quota impact.

Davin: one tricky bit: billing attribution. if enterprise requests fallback to free variant due to capacity, we must bill enterprise rates, not free. router must attach billing_metadata header even on fallback.

Priya: router header plan:
  - x-redwood-tier: <tier>
  - x-redwood-region: <region>
  - x-redwood-original-variant: <v2>
  - x-redwood-effective-variant: <v1>
  - x-redwood-fallback-reason: <oom|quota|backpressure>

Marisol: ops: can we add a short-term telemetry card to the console for the rollout window? need to see live fallback streams.

ops-bot: created dashboard `rollouts/staged-fanout/enterprise-paid-free` and added panel `fallback-rate by tier/region`.

Alex: code change proposal: router will accept a new config blob `rollout_policy_v2` with precompiled per-tier rules. control plane will push and sign it. fallback decision pseudocode in router:

```
if model_error or capacity_low:
  if counter[(tier,region,variant)] < max_fallback_rate*window:
    choose per_tier_target
    counter++
    attach headers
    return fallback
  else:
    return error or degrade differently
```

Davin: question — what should happen when per-tier target is itself behind capacity? chain fallback? limit chain depth to 1 or 2.

Priya: cap depth=1 for safety. if per-tier target fails, return error or route to a low-cost degraded path (sync to async): `fallback_mode: degrade_to_async`.

Marisol: action items:
- Priya: add `fallbacks_total` and label schema in telemetry PR (due EOD)
- Alex: open router PR for `rollout_policy_v2` + counters (due tomorrow)
- Davin: update control-plane push mechanism to sign blob per-tenant and add region overrides (due EOD)
- Ops: add live dashboard widgets and alert rules (in progress)

Davin: also pinging product for rollout windows so we can throttle if needed: @product-team

Marisol: thanks — keeping this thread as the canonical place for follow-ups. ping me for clarifications :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: rollout started: v2 -> enterprise(20%), paid(5%), free(1%) at 2025-11-02T14:30:00Z
